The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To explain the complex concepts of blockchain technology using an analogy:

Imagine a traditional bank ledger as a single, locked diary kept by one person (the bank). If that person makes a mistake or decides to cheat, it’s hard to prove because you can’t see the original entries easily.

Now, imagine blockchain as a **community notebook** shared among thousands of people. Every time a transaction happens, it’s written in this notebook. But here’s the key: everyone has their own copy of the notebook. Before a new page is added, the group must agree that the entry is correct. Once it’s written, it’s written in permanent ink—no one can erase or change it without everyone else noticing and rejecting the change. This makes the record incredibly secure and trustworthy because no single person controls it, and altering history would require changing every single copy simultaneously, which is practically impossible.
